column3: What went well and what went wrong, with a real root cause for each problem. Blameless: critique decisions and process, not people.
column6: 2 or more items on each side. Every problem names a specific cause, not a restatement of the problem. Nothing reads as blaming a teammate.
column9: Both sides present but thin, or causes are vague, or a problem is described without a cause.
column12: A list of good and bad things with no analysis of why.
column15: Missing, or the section blames individuals rather than examining process.

column3: Real numbers pulled from the repo (issues opened and closed, PRs opened and merged, stories planned against done) with working links, plus what you set out to build against what shipped.
column6: Counts are present, specific and match the repo. Links work. Planned against shipped is stated honestly.
column9: Some counts missing or clearly estimated, or some links do not work.
column12: No real numbers, or no working links.

column3: Complete sentences and complete ideas. Markdown headings so each required section is findable. Committed under docs/postmortem/ in the repo.
column6: Readable prose, clear headings, correct file layout in the repo.
column9: Understandable but sloppy: fragments, missing headings, or wrong file layout.
column12: Hard to follow, or not committed to the repo.

column3: Your individual file: your role and what you actually built, your biggest challenge with why it was hard and how you handled it, and the most valuable thing you learned. Graded per student.
column6: Present, specific to work you actually did, and answers every part in complete sentences.
column9: Present but generic, or skips one of the required parts.
column12: No section for you, or a section with no substance.

column3: Links to your own merged pull requests and your own issues. Graded per student.
column6: Links present and they resolve to work authored by you.
column9: Links present but incomplete, broken, or pointing at a teammate's work.

column3: Two things you will personally do differently in your next Project 02 team, each with how you will know it worked. Your P1 team is dissolving, so these are yours, not the team's. Graded per student.
column6: Two specific practices, each with a concrete check you could actually verify later.
column9: Commitments are vague, or only one is given, or there is no way to tell if it worked.
column12: Missing, or amounts to keep doing what I am doing.
